messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx / streaming disconnects detected for /v1/stream (us-west-2-hosted). Error rate spike 4.8% -> 12.3% over last 3m. Paging oncall: @alice

alice: acked. I'm oncall. brief status? any customer-facing errors?

ben: I just saw a PagerDuty page. Logs show a bunch of \"upstream connection reset by peer\" and 502/504 on our edge LB when streaming chunks are sent.

jamie: I'm looking at the runtime metrics. Streaming latency jumped and active connections dipped around the same time. Could be connection churn from clients cancelling mid-stream.

carol: customers reporting aborted streams and partial responses. One enterprise convo lost ~200 tokens midstream and client retried in a tight loop. That likely increased concurrency.

alice: initial mitigation I'll attempt: scale streaming workers + enable fallback to non-streaming (sync) for heavy customers to prevent token loss. Also can we enable the circuit-breaker to reject new streaming sessions above threshold?

eng-runtime: on it. Increasing replica count from 6 -> 10 in us-west-2. Pushing a temporary knob to reduce per-connection buffer size and extend keepalive to 60s.

jamie: looking at nginx edge logs:
```
2026-03-14T16:02:13Z 10.1.2.3 "GET /v1/stream" 502 0 "upstream prematurely closed connection"
2026-03-14T16:02:14Z 10.1.2.3 "GET /v1/stream" 504 0 "upstream timed out (110)"
```
Sequence: LB -> ingress proxy -> runtime. Upstream runtime is returning resets.

ben: any recent deploys? I see a runtime rollback in the morning but nothing right before spike. No model changes in prod in last 2h.

alice: rollouts: can we check kernel/quantization toggles? Those can increase memory pressure and OOM close. jamie?

jamie: checked pods: no OOMKilled events. Memory stable. But runtime threads are blocked waiting on socket write for some clients. Suspect some clients are cancelling and not reading, causing backpressure at our runtime write buffers -> writes fail.

carol: that matches customer reports — mobile SDKs sometimes close before full response when app backgrounded. A flurry of mobile cancels could cause too many half-closed sockets.

eng-runtime: implementing aggressive write timeouts and making socket writes non-blocking. Pushing a config to drop connections that don't drain within 250ms. Rolling in 2 mins.

alice: action: enable fallback to small sync responses for 5 top customers that reported the issue. whitelist IDs: cust-123, cust-omega, cust-alpha. Start now.

ben: done. Routing rule applied at edge to map those customers to /v1/generate-sync.

jamie: scaled runtime replicas completed. New pods healthy. Error rate now 9.6% down from 12.3%. Streaming disconnects still present but reduced.

carol: notified account teams for affected customers. First customer (cust-123) reported improvement after fallback. They still saw 1 aborted stream but it's lower.

alice: we should also check our LB idle timeout vs client keepalive. If LB is closing idle connections aggressively, chunked streaming can get cut. What are ELB timeouts?

eng-runtime: ELB idle timeout is 60s. Runtime keepalive was 30s. Bumping keepalive to 75s to match. Rolling config for edge proxies.

jamie: also enabling more aggressive KV cache reuse to reduce per-request compute and shorten stream durations for long completions. Might help throughput.

ben: telemetry note: add metric for "stream-chunk-write-failures" and client-cancel-rate by SDK version. This will help correlate mobile SDK cancels.

alice: good. I'll prepare a concise incident summary for handoff. Current impact: ~8-10% 5xx rate concentrated on /v1/stream endpoints in us-west-2. Mitigations applied: scaled replicas, enabled sync fallback for heavy customers, bumped keepalive, write timeouts. Partial recovery observed.

carol: customers impacted: cust-123 (enterprise), cust-omega (SaaS), cust-alpha (internal partner). Tickets created: #TCK-456, #TCK-457, #TCK-464. CS notified.

eng-runtime: config changes pushed: 
```
- runtime.relay.write_timeout_ms=250
- edge.keepalive_seconds=75
- runtime.replicas=10
- routing.fallback.sync_customers=[cust-123,cust-omega,cust-alpha]
```
Changes are reversible.

jamie: next steps: continue to monitor error rate and connection-reset logs for 30m. If >5% persist, revert to a safe runtime binary from last stable and cut a maintenance window.

alice: handing off to next oncall @ben for the midnight shift. Handoff summary: see above. Key open items: (1) monitor for 30m, (2) implement telemetry for chunk-write-failures, (3) follow up postmortem to determine client cancellation pattern + SDK update.

ben: ack. I'll keep watch and escalate if we regress. Please paste any debug commands or runbooks for me.

alice: debug commands saved in thread:
```
# check streaming errors
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n prod | rg "upstream prematurely closed|connection reset" --line-buffer
# inspect open sockets
kubectl exec -it runtime-pod -- ss -tan | rg ESTABLISHED | wc -l
# dump edge logs
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/edge/us-west-2/$(date +%F)/ --recursive --exclude "*" --include "edge.log*"
```
Also add to postmortem: ask product if prompt lengths have spiked for certain customers which could extend streaming durations.

incident-bot: Incident annotated. Severity: Sev2. Tags: streaming, 5xx, us-west-2, customer-impact.

ben: switching pager to night oncall. leaving monitoring checks in place. If anything flares, page with "streaming-regen".

alice: thanks team. I'll kick off the postmortem doc and include timeline + mitigations.

carol: noted. closing customer-facing comms draft and sending update to affected customers: "We applied temporary routing to reduce aborted streams and are actively investigating root cause. We'll follow-up with a permanent fix." :thumbsup:

ben: last_message:  monitoring window started. keeping channel open for further logs."
